overview.text: The University of Southern California (USC) is a private research university in Los Angeles, California. It opened in 1880, when Los Angeles was still a small frontier town, and grew from its first 53 students into a major institution with broad academic and research programs. Its sports teams are the Trojans, and USC’s athletic identity is especially visible through Traveler, a white horse ridden by a Trojan warrior at home football games; the tradition began in 1961. USC also has a notable athletic record, including a 26-year run of national team titles and a long Olympic history. USC officially joined the Big Ten Conference on August 2, 2024, alongside UCLA, Oregon and Washington.

key_facts.text: USC opened in 1880 with 53 students and 10 teachers.
USC describes itself as a private research university and links its work to Los Angeles and Southern California.
Traveler, the white horse ridden by a Trojan warrior, first appeared at USC football games in 1961.
USC’s Trojan teams won at least one national team title in 26 consecutive years, from 1959–60 through 1984–85.
USC became a Big Ten member on August 2, 2024, together with UCLA, Oregon and Washington.
